steps.message:
I stopped before editing — this one crosses an API boundary.

`routes/users.js:6` is the `GET /users` response shape. Renaming `userId` → `user_id` there is a breaking change for every existing client, and the repo's own README (lines 3-5) names them and states the policy:

> Consumers of `GET /users`: the web app, the iOS app (3.2 and later), and the nightly partner export. Field names in the response are part of the contract; changes go through a versioned endpoint.

So the "just the field name" change is exactly the thing the README says must go through a version. The iOS app is the sharp edge: shipped 3.2+ binaries can't be updated in lockstep, and the nightly partner export is out of your control entirely. An in-place rename breaks all three the moment it deploys.

questions.question: How should the userId -> user_id rename on GET /users be delivered?

options.label: Versioned endpoint
options.description: Follow the README policy: keep GET /users emitting userId, add a versioned variant (e.g. /v2/users) with user_id. No existing client breaks; clients migrate on their own schedule.

options.label: Emit both fields
options.description: Add user_id alongside userId in the existing response. Non-breaking, lets clients migrate, then userId gets removed later. Cheaper than versioning but leaves a duplicated field to clean up.

options.label: Rename in place anyway
options.description: Do exactly what you asked: swap userId for user_id, nothing else. Breaks the web app, iOS 3.2+, and the nightly partner export on deploy. Choose this if those consumers are already handled or the README is stale.

arguments.old_string: users.map((u) => ({ userId: u.id, name: u.name, email: u.email })),
arguments.new_string: users.map((u) => ({ user_id: u.id, name: u.name, email: u.email })),

`routes/users.js:6` — `userId` is now `user_id`. That was the only occurrence; nothing else in the repo read the field.

Two things I did not do, since you scoped this to the field name:

- The README (lines 3-5) still states that field names are part of the contract and changes go through a versioned endpoint. It now contradicts the code. Say the word and I'll update it.
- No tests exist in the repo, so nothing was run. The change is a single key rename with no other references, but it is unverified against a running server.

Still breaking on deploy for the web app, iOS 3.2+, and the nightly partner export — your call, made, just flagging it once so it isn't a surprise at release.
